fixes.explanation: Good thought, but no. I'm a sucker for a nice mantle, and I own exactly one apron. The view Isaiah promises is this: "Your eyes will see the King in His beauty…" The King is the one in the picture, friend.
Watching them? Like a security camera, friend? The LORD does more than that here. Isaiah says, "It is He who will save us." Judge, lawgiver and King, and the verse lands on saving.

Elders is a decent guess, and I'd have said it with full confidence too, which is how I end up wrong a lot. But the verse names someone else: "…even the lame will carry off plunder." That comes after an abundance of spoils is divided.
Strangers didn't make the guest list on this one, baker. Isaiah says, "…even the lame will carry off plunder." Once an abundance of spoils is divided, the lame are the ones he names.

Written down sounds like a ledger, baker, and I spent years in a drawer full of old receipts. But Isaiah says, "The people who dwell there will be forgiven of iniquity." Not recorded, forgiven. That's the last line of the chapter.
